text:
incident-bot: Incident created: KV cache pressure -> streaming stalls, elevated p95/p99 across usa region. Severity: P2.

alice: noticing big jump in streaming tail p99 starting ~15:20 UTC, correlates with increased prefill rates on a subset of shards. p95 up 2.3x, p99 up 6x.

ben: yup seeing same on grafana: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/streams/kvcache — main spike on kv-shard-12 and kv-shard-19.

carla: are there recent deploys? any autoscaler changes?

deploy-bot: deploy finished by emma at 15:09 UTC: infra/autoscaler: adjust-fill-concurrency -> 0.8 -> 1.2 (canary -> prod).

emma: that autoscaler change was intended to reduce cold-starts by allowing higher prefill concurrency. didn't expect to hit fragmentation case.

dan: quick summary of customer impact: some customers saw streaming stalls -> client timeouts at ~30s, ~4 customers reported partial transcripts missing. No billing issues.

frank: logs from a problematic host: ``[warn] kv_prefill_queue: dropped_prefill=312, eviction_for_prefill=180, decode_waiters=92`` — indicates prefill is contending with decode threads.

alice: hypothesis: prefill-heavy load increased slab fragmentation on those shards, causing frequent evictions and heavy decode/prefill imbalance. streaming requests (which rely on decode low-latency path) are getting starved -> tail stalls.

ben: reproduction plan: run a synthetic mix with elevated prefill concurrency against a single shard to see eviction rate. I have a job queued on perf cluster.

carla: mitigation ideas (short term):
- throttle prefill concurrency back to previous value (rollback autoscaler change)
- temporarily route streaming traffic to fallback model variant with looser memory profile
- increase slab size on affected shards (hotfixable?)

emma: I can rollback autoscaler in <5m. doing that now.

deploy-bot: rolling config rollback initiated by emma: autoscaler.pre-fill-concurrency -> 0.8 (targeted to region us-east-1).

alice: thanks. also enable eviction backoff: add 50ms backoff between prefill attempts on affected hosts. That should reduce eviction thrash.

frank: added a checkpoint script to move KV ownership for hot segments: `scripts/rebalance_kv --shard 12,19 --grace 30s` — but that is disruptive. prefer config changes first.

carla: we've got a canary patch ready that changes runtime priority: when a streaming session is active, decode threads get elevated priority over prefill (non-blocking prefill). patch ID: rti-2026-042. Want to promote to hotfix if rollback is insufficient.

dan: customers affected list: AcmeChat (streaming), BetaDocs (streaming + batch), InternalTestOrg (internal). outreach in progress, CS taking first contact.

alice: telemetry after rollback (5m): p95 dropped ~30%, p99 dropped ~45% on affected shards but still above SLO. some streaming stalls persist.

ben: logs show prefill attempts down but slab fragmentation still high: `slab_free_chunks=120, slab_total_chunks=1024, avg_chunk_size=8kb, fragmentation_ratio=0.64` — long-lived fragmentation.

emma: we should schedule a rolling restart of the runtime on the worst hosts to let allocator coalesce. low-risk rolling restart?

frank: agree — restart one host at a time, mark host out of rotation, drain in-flight. I'll prepare runbook: `runbooks/runtime/restart-host.md` with the drain steps.

carla: while we restart, let's enable the canary runtime priority patch on a single node to validate effect quickly. if that reduces tail stalls, we can promote cluster-wide.

alice: I'm going to add a temporary traffic-split rule: redirect 20% streaming traffic to fallback-small-model, to reduce load on prefill-heavy path. Config: `routes/streaming-split.yaml` applied.

deploy-bot: route change applied by alice at 15:47 UTC: streaming fallback 20% -> us-east-1.

dan: CS update: AcmeChat reduced timeouts after we split traffic; they still see 1/10 sessions with stalls, but overall degraded experience improved.

ben: perf job results (local perf cluster): prefill heavy workload triggers eviction waterfall when fragmentation_ratio > 0.55; enabling decode priority reduced tail latency by 65% in sim.

carla: promoted priority-patch to hotfix on single pool: patch applied to pool-az2-host-05. monitoring.

alice: after hotfix on that host we saw streaming tail p99 drop from 4.8s -> 1.6s for that host. good signal.

frank: starting rolling restarts to defragment slabs. will do 1 host every 7 minutes, check p99 between restarts.

emma: logging all mitigation steps in incident ticket INC-2026-309. linking to postmortem template.

incident-bot: Handoff reminder: on-call shift change at 18:00 UTC. Please post status and take Handoff.

alice: current status summary for handoff: autoscaler rollback done (15:22), 20% traffic split to fallback (15:47), priority hotfix applied to one host (15:55), rolling restarts in progress (started 16:02). p95 now within 1.2x SLO, p99 still ~1.8x SLO on a tiny fraction of sessions. CS notified. Next: finish restarts, promote priority patch, schedule allocator tuning.

ben: next action (post-incident): long-term fix options: slab allocator improvements, prefill backpressure mechanism (prefer backpressure vs aggressive prefill), shard-level compaction job, and autoscaler guardrails to detect fragmentation signals.

dan: leaving oncall in 30m — @carla will take over if ok.

carla: taking handoff. I'll continue restarts and coordinate with infra for a slab compaction job tomorrow.

alice: thanks all. I'll start drafting the incident postmortem with timeline + key metrics. saving logs: `s3://redwood-incidents/4098765432/`

frank: note: I captured heap + allocator profiles from 3 hosts and uploaded to the S3 bucket. will attach to the PM.

emma: thumbs up. any customer escalations beyond those three?

dan: no new escalations. monitoring still on high alert.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-309 status updated: mitigations applied, monitoring. Severity downgraded to P3 at 17:30 UTC.

carla: marking thread resolved for handoff but keeping alert channel open until restarts complete.

alice: final: action items created in Jira: RDW-4321 (allocator compaction), RDW-4322 (prefill backpressure), RDW-4323 (autoscaler guardrails).

ben: thanks team. :heart:

emma: great work. I'll follow up on postmortem draft.
